standard_prerequisites: topology on the set of points of an algebraic space and reduced induced closed subspace structures
proper, universally closed and separated morphisms of algebraic spaces and their behaviour under base change, composition and closed immersions

the standard morphism lemmas of Spaces quoted by the source (scheme-theoretic image of a proper morphism, image of universally closed over separated target, image of proper is proper, immersion locally of finite type, composition of finite type)
core_obligations: Prove the three functoriality clauses: images under separated-over-B maps or universally closed maps send closed subsets proper over B to closed subsets proper over B, and preimages under proper maps pull them back
proof_roadmap: (1) Put the reduced induced structure on T and apply the scheme-theoretic-image lemma for proper morphisms over B to the induced map into Y separated over B

(2) Factor the induced morphism Z to Z' through the scheme-theoretic inverse image Z''; Z'' to Z' is universally closed as a base change of f, the closed immersion Z to Z'' keeps universal closedness, so Z to Z' is universally closed and surjective

Conclude Z' to B is separated by the image lemma, quasi-compact from quasi-compactness of Z to B and surjectivity, locally of finite type from the immersion and composition lemmas, and universally closed from Z to B universally closed by the image-proper lemma
(3) The inverse image Z' = f^{-1}(Z) is proper over Z as a base change of the proper f, and properness over B follows by composition with Z to B
difficulty_reason: H2: three clause proofs, each an assembly of standard morphism lemmas; the middle clause is the longest with a factorisation and five quoted properties.
